Host: Welcome to the founder show. My guest today built a bootstrapped SaaS to eight
figures. Let's talk about how you prioritize.

Guest: The core method I use is what I call the ICE score. For every possible project,
you rate three things one to ten: Impact, how much it moves the metric that matters;
Confidence, how sure you are it'll work; and Ease, how little effort it takes. You
multiply them, sort descending, and you work the top of the list. It stops teams from
chasing shiny low-impact ideas.

Host: How often do you re-score?

Guest: Weekly. Scores decay as you learn. We also read The Lean Startup by Eric Ries
early on, and Obviously Awesome by April Dunford reshaped our positioning.

Host: Any hiring rule?

Guest: Hire slow on the first ten. We do a paid trial project before any full-time
offer. It's the single highest-leverage filter we found.
